news.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
paras: Last week, a hidden bug in Microsoft’s cloud gateway caused an outage. The bug made computer cores and memory stop working. Many businesses and schools lost access to Microsoft 365 and email for almost a full day.

The problem happened because three things lined up: a server update in July, sudden traffic changes, and weaker servers. When the new update ate too many CPU and memory resources, the servers crashed. Microsoft says this was a technical issue, not a cyber attack.

news.title: Comcast's "fiber-powered Wi-Fi" is just cable, AT&T says in false advertising case
paras: AT&T said Comcast lied about its internet. Comcast calls its cable Wi‑Fi “fiber‑powered”, but it uses cable, not true fiber, to reach homes. This makes customers think the service matches AT&T's fiber plans.

Because fiber brings equal upload and download speeds, the claim misleads customers. Most Xfinity roads use copper cables, so speeds are slower when sending data back. AT&T wants Comcast to pay for misleading ads. The lawsuit will force Comcast to correct its advertising and possibly pay compensation.

news.title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
paras: Put the cloud on the map Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity Study attempts to tally hyperscalers’ energy use and emissions. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers.

A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. news.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st in
paras: 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster .

The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from.

news.title: The Bloomsbury Group's Vanessa Bell and Duncan Grant Tangled Their Art and Lives Together for Decades. A Final
paras: The pair were central figures in the Bloomsbury Group , a circle of artists and intellectuals active in early 20th-century Britain who radically, and often controversially, challenged contemporary creative and social norms. These included public sentiments on philosophy, sexuality and mental illness. The group featured, among others, the economist John Maynard Keynes , as well as the writers E.

Forster and Virginia Woolf , Bell’s biological sister. Grant and Bell were often the subjects of each other’s work. Among their most well-known collaborations is one of Grant’s first and most extravagant depictions of Bell, a full-length portrait painted in 1915.

sport.title: How Maria Sharapova got on the year after winning the WTA Finals as Mirra Andreeva repeats feat
paras: What Mirra Andreeva has already accomplished at such a young age is astounding. At just 19 years of age, this year marked a standout for her, claiming her first Grand Slam title in Paris before capping the season off by winning the WTA Finals as well.

However, she is not the first teenage phenomenon to take the sport by storm, nor will she be the last. In fact, despite the hugely impressive nature of her WTA Finals triumph, she is still not the youngest to have ever won it. That title belongs to Maria Sharapova , a player who Mirra Andreeva likely would not mind following in the footsteps of.

sport.title: November 17, 1991: The day Pete Sampras claimed his first season-ending ATP Masters Cup
paras: On this day in tennis history, one young American beat a compatriot to win his first ATP Masters Cup. Look back on how he did it

On this day, November 17, 1991, in Frankfurt, Pete Sampras beat Jim Courier in the final (3-6, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4) to claim his first title at the season-ending Masters Cup . For the young American, who had lost his US Open crown two months earlier – to the same opponent – it was a relief to win such an important title after a hard season.
